title: Leading-window signature cache and soft-invalidation for embedding/rerank endpoint
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: The embeddings + rerank endpoint suffers from redundant compute and slower tail latency for short leading-context requests (search queries, chat turns). Current embedding cache is primarily full-vector keyed and misses frequently on partial or truncated inputs. We need a cache strategy that increases hit rate for short leading-context queries, reduces per-request embedding compute, and supports safe invalidation when underlying documents change.

Scope: implement a leading-window signature cache (cache keyed on a compact signature computed from the first N tokens / characters) combined with a content-signature tombstone approach for soft-invalidation. This ticket covers design, service-side implementation, integration with tenant routing, canary rollout, and evaluation against quality/regression tests. Does NOT include full UI in Console (follow-up ticket).

Goals:
- Increase embedding cache hit-rate for short leading-context requests by >= 2x on search workloads.
- Reduce median per-request embedding cost for small queries by ~25% for heavy-search customers.
- Keep rerank quality regressions under a strict threshold (mean reciprocal rank delta <= 0.5% on regression set).
- Provide a fast invalidation path so updated docs do not return stale reranks for more than 30s in the worst case for private deployments (configurable).
acceptance_criteria: Leading-window cache implemented as an additional fast-path: extract first 64 chars or first 6 tokens, compute 64-bit content signature, look up in L1 cache before full embed compute.
Cache hit-rate improvement demonstrated on staging: >=2x hit-rate on our search traffic replay against production traces.
End-to-end rerank regression tests run on evaluation harness with MRR delta <= 0.5%.

Soft-invalidation implemented using tombstone versions: document update writes tombstone with version id; cache entries tagged with version; stale entries evicted on mismatch or after tombstone window.
Canary: rollout to 10% of requests for two days with monitoring dashboards showing latency, hit-rate, cost delta, quality metrics.
Design and security review artifacts uploaded and approved.
decisions: Use a compact 64-bit rolling content-signature derived from FNV-1a + mixing rather than heavier simhash to minimize CPU overhead on hot path.
Cache key = tenant_id + model_variant + leading_window_signature + length_bucket to avoid cross-tenant leakage and reduce false hits across variants.
Soft-invalidation via tombstone versioning instead of immediate hard invalidation; tombstones include version id + expiry to allow fast invalidation without thrashing cache under burst updates.
Write-through for cold misses for top-traffic tenants (config flag), otherwise lazy populate to control write amplification.
Eviction policy: weighted recency-frequency (WRF) with normalization by token-length to prevent long queries from monopolizing cache slots.
Fallback: on approximate-match hits above similarity threshold, fallback to reranking flow that uses cached embedding as warm start (not full reliance).
comments: 2026-02-11 Aisha Patel: Initial spike complete — microbenchmark shows 3.1x signature compute/sec vs simhash on c5.large. Recording results in the design doc.
2026-02-12 Marco Ruiz: Implemented the signature function and local LRU prototype. Observed 18% p95 latency reduction on synthetic short-query workload.
2026-02-14 Design review (Liya Chen): suggested adding length_bucket to key to avoid mixing 1-token and 64-token vectors; agreed and updated key format.
2026-02-15 Security (Ravi Kumar): raised concern about tenant_id inclusion — confirmed we will never store tenant-sensitive identifiers in shared global cache; per-tenant namespace enforced.
2026-02-16 QA (Sofia Martinez): request to add rerank regression tests covering phrase-rewrites; added dataset and test pipeline in eval harness.
2026-02-17 Marco Ruiz: Opened PR #1249 for runtime changes (signature compute + cache hooks). Running internal integration tests.
2026-02-19 Aisha Patel: Canary started at 5% traffic for search-west cluster. Early metrics look good; hit-rate up 2.5x, p95 latency down 12% for leading-window requests.
2026-02-20 Liya Chen: Code review comments posted on PR about metrics naming and extra logs for invalidation events. Marco to address and re-request review.
notes: Implementation must be tolerant of variable tokenizers: use byte-level leading-window with optional tokenization fallback for model-specific variants.
For private deployments where global tombstone propagation may be slow, provide a configuration to reduce tombstone TTL and enable immediate push invalidation via control-plane hook.
Consider a follow-up ticket to expose cache stats per-tenant in Console (hit-rate, evictions, tombstone churn).
Risk: false positives on short, ambiguous leading windows could degrade quality for specific languages — mitigate with language-aware length thresholds and holdout tests.
